title: Internal HR-policy FAQ bot
brief: Employees ask questions about leave, benefits and holidays in a chat window. Answers must come from the 40-page HR handbook, which fits in a prompt. A person reads each answer immediately and asks a follow-up if needed.

evidence.next_step_controller: The employee decides the next step by typing the next question. The system never has to decide what to do after answering.
evidence.path_predictability: One question in, one grounded answer out. No intermediate findings change the plan.
evidence.reliability_need: Grounded in the handbook, but an employee double-checks anything important with HR.
evidence.cost_of_error: A wrong answer is embarrassing and correctable; nothing irreversible happens.
evidence.latency_budget: A person is waiting in a chat window.

tempting_wrong_answer: agentic ('it is a bot, so it is an agent')

title: Expense-report review against policy
brief: Every submitted expense report (free text plus attachments) is checked against the T&E policy and ends in exactly one of approve, reject or escalate-to-a-human. Finance audits a sample of decisions every month.

evidence.next_step_controller: Finance's written procedure decides the next step: read the claim, check the policy, decide, escalate if unsure. The steps are the same for every claim.
evidence.path_predictability: The branches are known in advance (approve, reject, escalate) and every violation code is in the policy. There is no discovery that changes the plan.
evidence.reliability_need: Auditors expect the same claim to get the same decision every time, with a reason they can replay.
evidence.cost_of_error: Paying a duplicate or non-compliant claim is real money and an audit finding.
evidence.latency_budget: Claims are processed in a queue; seconds to minutes are fine.

tempting_wrong_answer: agentic ('it calls tools, so it is an agent')

title: Nightly KPI digest email
brief: Every night at 02:00 pull yesterday's numbers from three dashboards, compare them with targets, write a three-paragraph plain-English summary and email it to 40 managers.

evidence.next_step_controller: A cron schedule and a fixed script decide every step: fetch, compare, summarise, send.
evidence.path_predictability: Exactly the same four steps every night. Only the data changes.
evidence.reliability_need: Managers expect it every morning, formatted the same way. A missed or mangled email is noticed.
evidence.cost_of_error: A mediocre summary is a small annoyance; numbers come from code, not from the model.

tempting_wrong_answer: agentic ('it fetches data from three tools')

title: Open-ended competitive research question
brief: A strategy analyst asks: 'How is Rival Corp positioning its new product line against us in the mid-market, and what is our weakest flank?' Nobody knows in advance which sources, how many searches, or which follow-up questions will matter.

evidence.next_step_controller: What to search next depends on what the last search found. Only the model can pick the next step at run time.
evidence.path_predictability: Open ended. The number and order of steps cannot be listed in advance.
evidence.reliability_need: The output is input to a human's thinking, not a record of fact; different valid reports are acceptable.
evidence.cost_of_error: A weak report costs an analyst some time; she reviews it before anything is decided.
evidence.latency_budget: Minutes are acceptable for a research brief.

title: Production-incident triage across logs, runbooks and paging
brief: An alert fires at 3 a.m. The system must work out what is broken by reading logs, metrics and runbooks, form a hypothesis, test it with more queries, and decide whom to page. Every incident looks different.

evidence.next_step_controller: Each query is chosen from what the previous query revealed (hypothesis, test, revise). No fixed procedure covers every incident.
evidence.path_predictability: Open ended: the investigation path differs per incident.
evidence.reliability_need: On-call engineers rely on it; it must not hallucinate evidence. That is a reason for guardrails, not for a fixed script.
evidence.cost_of_error: Paging the wrong team or missing a real outage is expensive and public.
evidence.latency_budget: Minutes matter, but a few seconds per step is fine.

tempting_wrong_answer: conversational ('just have it summarise the alert')
